title.value: Probabilistic Surrogate Networks for Simulators with Unbounded Randomness
title.justification: The title 'Probabilistic Surrogate Networks for Simulators with Unbounded Randomness' directly references the focus of the paper on creating surrogate models for stochastic simulators.
title.quote: Probabilistic Surrogate Networks for Simulators with Unbounded Randomness

extractions.description: This paper presents a novel framework for developing deep neural surrogates for stochastic simulators with potentially unbounded randomness. The surrogates, called probabilistic surrogate networks (PSNs), retain the structure and control flow of the original simulator, allowing for faster simulations and accurate inference. The surrogates are especially beneficial for scenarios requiring numerous iterations of the simulators, such as materials quality testing in composite manufacturing. The framework enables faster simulation and posterior inference by employing PSNs in conjunction with neural network-based inference compilation.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on surrogate modeling for general stochastic simulators and its applications, such as materials testing in manufacturing processes. It does not specifically address Climate Change topics or goals.
climate_change_is_central.quote: Specifically, we do simulator-based materials quality testing, inferring safety-critical latent internal temperature profiles of composite materials undergoing curing.

secondary_categories.quote: The fidelity and speed of our surrogates allow for both faster stochastic simulation and accurate and substantially faster posterior inference.
